title: Repeal clean energy spending laws and rescind unspent funds
proposal: The chapter supports repealing the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act and the Inflation Reduction Act, which fund renewable energy programs. It also supports taking back all of their money that has not yet been spent.
quote: to renewable energy developers, their investors, and special interests, and support the rescinding of all funds not already spent by these programs.

title: Rename DOE the Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science
proposal: The chapter recommends renaming the Department of Energy as the Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science (DESAS). It would focus on energy security, energy interests abroad, basic science, nuclear cleanup, and nuclear weapons and naval reactors.
quote: The Department of Energy should be renamed and refocused as the Department of Energy Security and Advanced Science (DESAS).

title: Raise DOE's energy security office to Assistant Secretary level
proposal: The chapter recommends making the Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response an Assistant Secretary-level office, reporting to a new Undersecretary of Energy Security.
quote: Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER), elevated to an Assistant Secretary.

title: Drop carbon management from the Office of Fossil Energy
proposal: The chapter recommends removing carbon management from the name and purpose of the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management. It would return to its original name and mission of increasing energy security and supply through fossil fuels.
quote: Office of Fossil Energy (Assistant Secretary, with Carbon Management deleted from its title and purpose.

title: Eliminate or reform DOE clean energy funding offices
proposal: The chapter recommends eliminating or reforming several DOE funding offices, including the Office of State and Community Energy Programs. It says these offices act as subsidies for favored energy sources.
quote: Office of Grid Deployment (OGD); and DOE Loan Program should be eliminated or reformed.

title: Speed natural gas export approvals without climate review
proposal: The chapter recommends removing political and climate-change factors from DOE approvals of liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports. It calls for quick approvals and keeping or restoring an environmental review exemption for LNG exports.
quote: Eliminate political and climate-change interference in DOE approvals of liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports.

title: Extend automatic natural gas export approvals to all U.S. allies
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress change the Natural Gas Act so automatic LNG export approvals cover all U.S. allies, such as NATO countries, not just free trade partners.
quote: to expand required approvals from merely nations with free trade agreements to all of our allies, such as NATO countries.

title: Stop requiring federal buildings to buy renewable energy
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Federal Energy Management Program focus on reliable, low-cost energy for federal buildings and stop pushing purchases of more expensive energy for climate reasons. It says agencies should follow a 2018 executive order on cutting waste and costs.
quote: FEMP should stop using taxpayer dollars to force the purchase of more expensive and less reliable energy resources in the name of combating climate change.

title: Streamline nuclear licensing rules
proposal: The chapter recommends simplifying nuclear regulatory requirements and licensing to lower costs and speed up new reactors, including small modular reactors.
quote: Streamline the nuclear regulatory requirements and licensing process. Such changes would help to lower costs

title: End energy justice, Justice40 and DEI programs at DOE
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE stop using energy policy for social agendas, naming programs such as energy justice, Justice40 and DEI. It says employees should be managed based on talent and work.
quote: The next Administration should stop using energy policy to advance politicized social agendas.

title: Write a National Energy Security Strategy
proposal: The chapter recommends that the renamed department study U.S. international energy interests and write a National Energy Security Strategy to advise the President. It says the strategy should not become a tool for industrial or climate policy.
quote: DESAS should analyze U.S. international energy security interests and develop a National Energy Security Strategy (NESS).

title: Give DOE a bigger role on the National Security Council
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE's international affairs chief support the Secretary on National Security Council work. DOE officials should have seats at senior NSC meetings and NSC staff positions like other national security agencies.
quote: The existing Assistant Secretary for International Affairs should provide the principal support for the DOE Secretary and Deputy Secretary on National Security Council (NSC) activities

title: Focus national labs on basic research
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE's 14 science and energy labs focus on basic research and leave technology demonstration and deployment to private companies. It also calls for working with Congress to cut duplication across the lab network.
quote: The remaining 14 science and energy labs should focus on basic research projects; demonstration and deployment of technology should be left to the private sector.

title: Review and consolidate all federal science agencies
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing all federal science agencies, including the expansion of the National Science Foundation's mission. It also calls for ranking and combining DOE programs.
quote: Before the start of a new Administration, there should be a review of all the federal science agencies.

title: Give private industry more responsibility for nuclear waste
proposal: The chapter recommends a new approach that gives the private sector more responsibility for disposing of nuclear waste. This includes amending the Nuclear Waste Policy Act to allow market pricing and competition for waste services.
quote: Develop a new approach that increases the level of private-sector responsibility for the disposal of nuclear waste.

title: Fund new nuclear warheads and plutonium pit production
proposal: The chapter recommends funding the design, development and deployment of new nuclear warheads, including large-scale production of plutonium pits.
quote: Fund the design, development, and deployment of new nuclear warheads, including the production of plutonium pits in quantity.

title: Expand the Navy and develop new naval nuclear reactors
proposal: The chapter recommends expanding the U.S. Navy and developing new nuclear reactors to power its ships.
quote: Expand the U.S. Navy and develop new nuclear naval reactors to ensure that the Navy has the nuclear propulsion it needs

title: End some nonproliferation work, including with Iran and the UN
proposal: The chapter recommends ending nonproliferation activities it calls ineffective, such as those involving Iran and the United Nations.
quote: End ineffective and counterproductive nonproliferation activities like those involving Iran and the United Nations.

title: Bring back the order securing the power grid from foreign equipment
proposal: The chapter recommends reinstating a version of Executive Order 13920, which aimed to secure the bulk power grid, including against risky foreign equipment.
quote: A good first step would be to reinstate an iteration of the Trump Administration's Executive Order 13920

title: Merge the Office of Electricity with the energy security office
proposal: The chapter suggests combining DOE's Office of Electricity with the cybersecurity and energy security office, along with any remaining parts of the Grid Deployment Office.
quote: OE could be combined with CESER (as well as what is left of the Grid Deployment Office if it is eliminated).

title: Eliminate Office of Electricity grant programs
proposal: The chapter recommends ending Office of Electricity grants for things like energy storage and grid technology testing, and working with Congress to end DOE applied energy and commercial deployment funding.
quote: work with Congress to eliminate all DOE applied energy programs including OE (except perhaps those related to basic science for new energy technology).

title: Shrink the Office of Nuclear Energy to basic research
proposal: The chapter recommends limiting the Office of Nuclear Energy's size and scope to basic research and waste issues. It should start no new commercial reactor demonstration projects and leave commercial support to the private sector.
quote: NE should transition to a more limited scope of responsibilities that focuses on basic research, solving broadly applicable technology challenges

title: Reorganize nuclear energy office into three lines of work
proposal: The chapter recommends organizing the Office of Nuclear Energy's remaining work into nuclear fuels, reactor technology and civilian radioactive waste.
quote: Reorganize its remaining activities into three basic lines of responsibility: nuclear fuels across the fuel cycle, reactor technology, and civilian radioactive waste.

title: End DOE carbon capture programs
proposal: The chapter recommends eliminating DOE's carbon capture, utilization and storage programs and leaving that work to private companies.
quote: CCUS programs should be left to the private sector to develop.

title: Pursue critical minerals from coal waste
proposal: The chapter recommends pursuing the processing of critical minerals from coal mining and combustion waste for national security.
quote: reserves of coal and abundant waste from coal mining and combustion, should be pursued.

title: Eliminate the Office of Fossil Energy and Carbon Management
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to eliminate DOE's applied energy programs, including the fossil energy office, except perhaps basic science. If it remains, its funding should target energy security and supply.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to eliminate all of DOE's applied energy programs, including those in FECM

title: Keep the Strategic Petroleum Reserve for emergencies only
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Strategic Petroleum Reserve be kept for national strategic purposes and not used for political gain.
quote: the new DESAS should ensure that the SPR is maintained for national strategic purposes and not misused for political gain.

title: Repeal or loosen appliance energy efficiency standards
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to change or repeal the law requiring energy efficiency standards for appliances. Until then, DOE should focus on the few rules that save the most energy and avoid rules that hurt product quality.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to modify or repeal the law mandating energy efficiency standards.

title: Eliminate the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to eliminate DOE's applied energy programs, including the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, except perhaps basic science.
quote: work with Congress to eliminate all of DOE's applied energy programs, including those in EERE

title: Cut renewable energy office funding and rescind unspent money
proposal: If the office is not eliminated, the chapter recommends cutting its budget and having Congress take back unspent funds. Any remaining money should go to basic research rather than deployment.
quote: It should rescind these excess monies so that DOE is not required to spend them.

title: Eliminate the Grid Deployment Office
proposal: The chapter recommends eliminating DOE's Grid Deployment Office and moving any needed reliability work to the energy security office.
quote: Eliminate GDO and assign necessary activities to the reformed CESER.

title: Consider ending nuclear and hydropower subsidies from the 2021 law
proposal: The chapter suggests considering whether to stop funding the civil nuclear credit program and hydropower incentives from the infrastructure law. It notes these may need to continue if renewable subsidies are not repealed.
quote: Consider whether to defund the civil nuclear tax credit program and hydroelectric power efficiency and production incentives established in the IIJA

title: End DOE's role in planning power lines for renewables
proposal: The chapter recommends ending DOE's role in grid planning, such as national transmission studies and corridors, that it says mainly benefits renewable energy developers.
quote: End DOE/GDO's role in grid planning for the benefit of renewable developers.

title: Defund most grid programs and rescind unspent money
proposal: The chapter recommends defunding most Grid Deployment Office programs, which oversee nearly $20 billion from the infrastructure law, and having Congress take back money not yet spent.
quote: Defund most GDO programs. GDO oversees nearly $20 billion in new appropriations created by the IIJA

title: Eliminate the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to end all DOE energy demonstration programs, including the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, and cutting its staff.
quote: work with Congress to eliminate all DOE energy demonstration programs, including those in OCED.

title: Stop new DOE energy loans and close the Loan Programs Office
proposal: The chapter recommends making no new DOE loans or loan guarantees and asking Congress to end DOE's lending authority and eventually close the Loan Programs Office.
quote: Should seek to sunset DOE's loan authority through Congress and eventually eliminate the Loan Program Office.

title: Limit any remaining DOE loans to grid reliability and security
proposal: If loan programs continue, the chapter recommends stronger checks and more openness, and limiting new loans to projects that support grid reliability and national security.
quote: Limit the use of new loan or loan guarantee authority to projects that will promote the reliability and resilience of the electric grid

title: Add forced-labor and double-subsidy rules for DOE loan applicants
proposal: The chapter recommends requiring loan applicants to follow the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act and certify they have no other government-backed loans or bonds, such as from state green banks.
quote: certify that they are not financed with any other local, state, or federal taxpayer-backed loan, loan guarantee, or bond

title: Eliminate ARPA-E
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress to eliminate the Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy, which funds early energy technology.
quote: The next Administration should work with Congress to eliminate ARPA–E. The agency is unnecessary, risks taxpayer dollars

title: Eliminate the Clean Energy Corps
proposal: The chapter recommends ending the Clean Energy Corps by cutting its funding and eliminating all jobs filled under the program.
quote: Eliminate the Clean Energy Corps by revoking funding and eliminating all

title: Count backup power costs when comparing wind and solar
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Energy Information Administration include the cost of backup power for wind and solar when comparing the costs of power sources.
quote: The cost of backup power for when wind and solar resources are not available should be included when comparing the technologies

title: Change how grid reserve margins are calculated
proposal: The chapter recommends that EIA, FERC, NERC and grid operators redefine grid reserve margins to cover all hours of the day and year. Wind, solar and other non-dispatchable sources might be left out of the calculation.
quote: should change how electric grid reserve margins are defined and calculated.

title: Publish regular reports on federal energy subsidies
proposal: The chapter recommends that EIA report on federal energy subsidies every year or two as a regular part of its work.
quote: This report should become a project that is performed annually or every other year as part of EIA's base program.

title: Base EIA world energy forecasts only on current law
proposal: The chapter recommends that EIA's International Energy Outlook forecasts be based on current laws and rules, not on favored policies.
quote: EIA forecasts should be based on current laws and regulations and should not be used to promote favored policies.

title: Study privatizing the Energy Information Administration
proposal: The chapter suggests assessing whether to privatize EIA, weighing cost savings against the value of its neutral data.
quote: Assess the case for privatization. There are some who think that EIA should be privatized.

title: Eliminate State's energy bureau and move its work to DOE
proposal: The chapter recommends putting international energy work under DOE's Office of International Affairs and eliminating the State Department's Bureau of Energy Resources, with DOE staff replacing its posts abroad.
quote: International energy activities should be consolidated under IA (and the Department of State's Bureau of Energy Resources should be eliminated)

title: Refuse to pay climate reparations
proposal: The chapter recommends not supporting climate reparations to developing countries in any form. It says the President should refuse to pay them under an unratified treaty and DOE should urge other countries to reconsider.
quote: A reparations slush fund administered by a non-U.S. organization provides no assurance that U.S. interests will be protected and should not be supported in any form.

title: Set a U.S. strategy for the Arctic and Alaska energy
proposal: The chapter recommends defining U.S. strategic and economic interests in the Arctic, including threats from Russia and China, and planning the development of Alaska's energy resources.
quote: The United States must establish a strategic plan to promote its national security, energy, and economic interests in the Arctic.

title: Expand the Arctic Energy Office and give it Antarctic duties
proposal: The chapter recommends expanding the Arctic Energy Office's work in Alaska to include rare earths, oil and gas, making it lead for DOE in Antarctica, and naming a senior energy official to the Arctic Council delegation.
quote: AE's operations in Alaska should be expanded to encompass broader national energy security interests in the region including rare earths, oil, and natural gas.

title: Have DOE intelligence office report directly to the Secretary
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE's Office of Intelligence and Counterintelligence be led by a qualified appointee with intelligence experience who reports directly to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary.
quote: IAC should be led by a qualified appointee and report directly to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary.

title: Keep DOE-funded technology in American hands
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE's Office of Technology Transitions protect taxpayer-funded research from espionage and make sure new technologies go to American businesses when commercialized.
quote: For security and economic espionage reasons, the work funded by the American people needs to be protected, and when commercialized, it needs to go to American businesses.

title: Make national labs more accountable to DOE and Congress
proposal: The chapter recommends making the National Laboratories more directly accountable to the Secretary of Energy and Congress for their work and management.
quote: The National Laboratories need to be more directly accountable to the Secretary of Energy and Congress for their work and management.

title: Return profits from lab technologies to taxpayers
proposal: The chapter recommends improving private access to National Labs while making sure money earned from taxpayer-funded technology flows back to taxpayers, such as through patent sharing or a revolving fund.
quote: ensuring that the economic benefits of taxpayer-funded technologies flow back to taxpayers through patent-review sharing or a revolving fund.

title: Speed up nuclear weapons site cleanup to finish by 2035
proposal: The chapter recommends considering a 10-year program to finish cleanup of all Cold War nuclear sites by 2035, except Hanford by 2060. It says this would need more cleanup funding in the short term.
quote: a 10-year program to complete all sites by 2035 (except Hanford with a target date of 2060) should be considered.

title: Apply the High-Level Waste rule across DOE cleanup sites
proposal: The chapter recommends fully applying the High-Level Waste determination across DOE sites, especially Hanford, so low-level waste can be grouted instead of turned into glass.
quote: Fully adopting the High-Level Waste (HLW) determination across the DOE complex, particularly at Hanford, would allow LLW to be grouted rather than vitrified.

title: Use more commercial nuclear waste disposal sites
proposal: The chapter recommends using commercial disposal sites more often to cut costs and speed cleanup.
quote: Increase the use of commercial waste disposal. Using commercial disposal would reduce capital costs

title: Revisit the Hanford cleanup agreement
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE and EPA work together to seek changes to the Hanford cleanup agreement with Washington State, including action by Congress if needed.
quote: DOE and EPA need to work more closely to coordinate their responses to claims made under the TPA and work more aggressively for changes

title: Make the cleanup office report more directly to the Deputy Secretary
proposal: The chapter recommends more direct leadership of the Office of Environmental Management by the Deputy Secretary, as the Government Accountability Office suggested.
quote: Establish more direct leadership and accountability to the Deputy Secretary consistent with Government Accountability Office recommendations.

title: Restart Yucca Mountain nuclear waste licensing
proposal: The chapter recommends that DOE restart the licensing process for the Yucca Mountain nuclear waste site and look for a second repository site.
quote: Restart Yucca Mountain licensing. DOE should restart the Yucca Mountain licensing process.

title: Use consent-based siting to build nuclear waste sites
proposal: The chapter recommends using the consent-based siting process to actually pick and build temporary or permanent sites for civilian nuclear waste.
quote: use the consent-based-siting process to identify and build temporary or permanent sites for a civilian waste nuclear repository

title: Let nuclear plant operators control waste disposal funds
proposal: The chapter recommends new funding and accounting methods for the Nuclear Waste Fund so licensed nuclear operators can set aside money for waste disposal while keeping control of it.
quote: Develop new NWF funding and accounting mechanisms that allow licensed nuclear operators to guarantee resources for future nuclear waste disposal

title: Re-create the Office of Civilian Radioactive Waste Management
proposal: The chapter recommends bringing back the nuclear waste office created by law, with its own Director. It would plan next steps on Yucca Mountain and manage the Nuclear Waste Fund and related funds.
quote: OCRWM, as already established by statute, should be tasked with developing the next steps on Yucca Mountain and nuclear waste management.

title: Keep the B83 bomb and the sea-launched nuclear cruise missile
proposal: The chapter recommends new warheads for each part of the nuclear triad. It calls for reversing decisions to retire the B83 bomb and cancel the submarine-launched cruise missile, if possible.
quote: reverse the Biden Administration's decision to retire the B83 bomb (in order to maintain two aircraft-delivered warheads) and its decision to cancel

title: Keep two plutonium pit factories
proposal: The chapter recommends keeping two sites for making plutonium pits, a key part of nuclear warheads, at Los Alamos and Savannah River.
quote: Maintain two production sites for plutonium pits (a key element of warhead production) at Los Alamos and Savannah River.

title: Reject the nuclear test ban treaty and prepare for tests
proposal: The chapter recommends rejecting ratification of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty and being willing to test nuclear weapons if adversaries' actions call for it. NNSA would be told to get ready to test quickly.
quote: Reject ratification of the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty and indicate a willingness to conduct nuclear tests in response to adversary nuclear developments

title: Review ship programs for possible nuclear power
proposal: The chapter recommends that the Director of Naval Reactors review new Navy, Homeland Security and Maritime Administration ship programs for possible use of nuclear reactors.
quote: Review all new Navy, Department of Homeland Security, and U.S. Department of Transportation Maritime Administration construction programs.

title: Cut non-defense work at nuclear weapons labs
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing non-national security work at Los Alamos, Lawrence Livermore and Sandia labs and dropping some of it to focus on nuclear deterrence.
quote: Review the non–national security portfolios at the Los Alamos, Lawrence Livermore, and Sandia labs and identify divestments to focus on nuclear deterrence.

title: Review the Nuclear Weapons Council
proposal: The chapter recommends reviewing how the Nuclear Weapons Council works so it provides fuller oversight of DOE and Defense nuclear weapons policy.
quote: Review the operations of the Nuclear Weapons Council (NWC). The statutorily established NWC is required to report to the President and Congress

title: Shift DOE non-nuclear money to nuclear weapons work
proposal: The chapter recommends using money from DOE's non-nuclear programs first to pay for more nuclear weapons work at NNSA.
quote: DOE non-nuclear programs should be the first source of additional resources for NNSA activities.

title: Require wind and solar to arrange backup power in grid markets
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC direct regional grid operators to pay extra for reliable power plants or require wind and solar to buy backup power. Other options include separate markets for reliable and intermittent power.
quote: FERC should direct RTOs to establish reliability pricing for eligible dispatchable generation resources or require intermittent resources to procure backup power

title: Repeal subsidies for power generation
proposal: The chapter recommends that Congress repeal subsidies for electricity generation sources.
quote: when they are not available to operate. In addition, Congress should repeal subsidies for generation resources.

title: Weigh gas pipelines' role in grid reliability
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC consider natural gas's role in electric reliability when reviewing pipeline applications, and that grid pricing support power plants that buy firm gas service.
quote: FERC needs to ensure that its consideration of natural gas pipeline applications recognizes the role that natural gas plays in electric reliability.

title: End grid market rules that disadvantage coal, gas and nuclear
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC change market rules that unfairly disadvantage dispatchable power such as coal, gas and nuclear, and stop subsidized sources from distorting prices.
quote: FERC should reform market rules that unduly discriminate against dispatchable resources needed for reliability.

title: Ban Chinese-made grid parts and harden substations
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC and NERC improve power grid security, for example by banning Chinese-made parts, investing in transformers and hardening substations.
quote: enhance the security of the bulk power system by, for example, banning Chinese-made components, investing in transformers, and hardening substations

title: Reexamine regional grid operators
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC reexamine the regional transmission organizations it oversees to make sure they buy reliable and affordable electricity.
quote: FERC needs to reexamine the RTOs under its jurisdiction to make sure that they procure reliable and affordable electricity

title: Pass renewable cost savings on to electricity customers
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC direct grid operators to make sure savings from renewables, such as tax credits and no fuel costs, reach customers.
quote: Direct the RTOs to ensure that the economic benefits of renewables (like tax credits and no fuel costs) are passed on to customers.

title: Let states decide whether to join regional grid operators
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC confirm states can choose whether to join a regional grid operator and consider letting states form other kinds of power pools.
quote: Affirm its commitment that states will decide whether to join an RTO instead of imposing RTOs on regions that do not want them.

title: Stop spreading new power line costs to customers who don't benefit
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC make transmission planning neutral among energy sources and not spread line costs to customers who do not benefit or justify them by climate goals. It also says national transmission corridors should respect states.
quote: Prevent socializing costs for customers who do not benefit from the projects or justifying such cost shifts as advancing vague “societal benefits” such as climate change.

title: Approve gas pipelines based only on need
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC limit its decisions on natural gas pipeline permits to whether the gas is needed.
quote: Limit its NGA decision-making on natural gas pipeline certificates to the question of whether there is a need for the natural gas.

title: Limit pipeline environmental reviews to the pipeline itself
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC's environmental reviews of pipelines look only at the pipeline's own impacts, not upstream or downstream effects such as greenhouse gas emissions.
quote: Limit its NEPA analysis to the impacts of the actual pipeline itself, not indirect upstream and downstream effects.

title: Better protect landowners whose property is taken for pipelines
proposal: The chapter suggests that Congress, the states and FERC consider better ways to protect and pay property owners whose land is taken for pipelines.
quote: and compensate property owners whose property is taken for the benefit of the public.

title: Don't use climate change to block LNG export terminals
proposal: The chapter recommends that FERC not use climate change or similar environmental issues as reasons to stop LNG export projects, and that needed pipelines be reviewed and built on time.
quote: Should not use environmental issues like climate change as a reason to stop LNG projects.

title: Set deadlines for nuclear license reviews
proposal: The chapter recommends that the NRC finish reviews of light-water reactor licenses and design certifications within about two years, and early site permits at existing sites within about one year.
quote: Applications for Combined Operating Licenses (COLs) and design certifications that rely on light-water technology should generally be completed within two years.

title: Speed up license extensions for existing nuclear plants
proposal: The chapter recommends that the NRC speed up approval of license extensions for existing reactors by streamlining its environmental reviews.
quote: Expedite the review and approval of license extensions of existing reactors, which will require the NRC to streamline and focus its NEPA review process.

title: Replace the ALARA radiation principle with fixed standards
proposal: The chapter recommends dropping the "as low as reasonably achievable" (ALARA) principle for radiation exposure and setting clear standards based on risk and dose.
quote: Set clear radiation exposure and protection standards by eliminating ALARA (“as low as reasonably achievable”) as a regulatory principle

title: Change how the NRC is funded
proposal: The chapter recommends working with Congress so license holders pay fees only for work specific to them, with other NRC costs paid through regular appropriations.
quote: Work with Congress to reform its funding approach so that licensee fees are generally required for activities that are specific to a regulated entity
